references.text: The parallel account in Matthew about the large herd of pigs grazing nearby, and the demons' request to be sent into the pigs.
The parallel account in Mark about the large herd of pigs grazing on the hillside, and the demons' request for permission to enter the pigs, which Jesus granted them.
In the Mosaic Law, the pig is declared an unclean animal, which explains why a herd of pigs was present in this pagan region.
The pig is considered unclean under the Mosaic Law, providing context that pig farming was associated with pagan/non-Jewish culture in the area where the event took place.
The demons asked Jesus not to send them into the abyss (v. 31), and in this verse they instead request permission to enter the herd of pigs—Jesus grants their request.
The continuation of the account where the demons enter the pigs, causing the herd to rush down a steep cliff and drown in the sea.
The theme of God's sovereign power over evil spirits is reflected in Jesus granting the demons permission—a parallel to the final exercise of authority over Satan and his forces.
